history.period: legendary; present small temple is modern
history.summary: Shree Rukmani Kund is a sacred spring-fed pool in the Shivalik hills, about 28 km from Bilaspur town, with a small temple at its edge. Local legend says Rukmani offered herself in sacrifice during a severe drought, after which a life-giving spring appeared at her feet; the pool is said never to dry and its waters are believed to have healing qualities. A fair (mela) in her name has been held here for some years; the site was selected under the Har Gaon Ki Kahani programme for 2012-2013 and supplies drinking water to nearby villages. (verify) The site is thinly documented - most coverage comes from travel blogs and Wikipedia rather than official tourism sources. CSV town 'Bilaspur' corrected to actual locality Salasi (near Auhar).

name: Rukmani Kund Temple
town_description: Salasi is a small village in Bilaspur district, Himachal Pradesh, in the Shivalik hills about 28 km from Bilaspur town on the Bhager-Gehrwin-Auhar road; the kund is reached by rural tracks from Auhar, the last bus stop.

travel.road: Road from Bilaspur via Bhager-Gehrwin toward Auhar; last public transport stop is Auhar, then a private vehicle or walk on kuccha road

visitor_information.opening_hours: Open-access site; typically visited in daylight hours (no published temple timings) (verify)
